deltas: Layered strategy/layer contract with EvaluateLayers/PlanStrategy/capability table and honest PipelineVerdict

Three gateway adapters: PCP (strong nonce ownership, RFC 6887 24-byte wire, PREFER_FAILURE, epoch tracking with cross-transaction baseline), NAT-PMP (weak lease ownership, RFC 6886 delete semantics), UPnP IGD (interface-bound SSDP, scoped description, redirect-refusing SOAP, bounded candidate retry, query-then-delete, strict-port enforcement)
direct-v4 and manual-static layers; manual endpoint validation shared by manager and manual.Layer
DefaultRouteSource: gateway strategies map the default-route interface's own (private) IPv4; Assess stays global-only for direct-v4
Node detection (bounded parallel, temp-tuple hygiene, UDP deferred), traversal profile with fingerprint staleness, mapping journal with serialized mechanism-private State

Per-Forward Manager: acquisition composition, same-tuple STUN seam (StunObserveRequest{Server,Bind,Dial}), §3.5 renewal ladder (DEGRADED at 3 failures; LOST at granted-lease expiry safety margin / confirmed reboot / rewritten external endpoint), lifecycle dispatcher off the renewal goroutine, idempotent Release that preserves the journal record on failed gateway deletes
stun.LeaseSource + NewManagerObserver: shared-port same-tuple observation wiring for the manager
netns TCP traversal lab: Manager-driven end-to-end against real miniupnpd 2.3.4 and coturn with independent vantage verification and post-release closed-port verification
behavioral_summary: A forward with an explicit-gateway strategy acquires the listener on the default-route interface's own address, maps it through the detected mechanism, optionally observes the same tuple via STUN, journals the mapping with honest ownership and renewal state, renews near 50% of the GRANTED lease, degrades after three consecutive renewal failures, loses only at the expiry safety margin / confirmed reboot / rewritten endpoint, and releases with ownership-strength deletion that leaves the journal record in place whenever the gateway delete failed.

known_limits: No real CPE/router inventory exists: the gateway adapters are validated against miniupnpd 2.3.4 (PCP+NAT-PMP+IGDv2) and coturn in a Linux netns lab only, and remain experimental per the frozen support matrix. miniupnpd does not implement PCP §8.2 source-address checking (the lab cannot exercise the ADDRESS_MISMATCH path that unit tests pin).

The lab vantage sits inside the lab topology (11.0.0.1); nothing here is public-WAN evidence, and no public-WAN claim is made. The lab CPE WAN address (11.0.0.2) classifies GLOBAL_PUBLIC because 11/8 is not RFC1918 - correct per the frozen rules.

Same-tuple STUN observation through the real NAT is verified at address level (observed address == CPE WAN). Observed-port agreement with the mapping port is daemon-specific (equal for miniupnpd's PCP/NAT-PMP paths, masqueraded for UPnP) and is not asserted.
The renewal ladder's margin/reboot/endpoint-rewrite paths are pinned by unit tests with scripted mappers; no real gateway reboot was exercised in the lab.

Crash window: a successful mapper.Map before journalPut leaves a gateway mapping without a durable record (no intent-record semantics in JournalStore). Declared as P14 recovery input; the journalized State (PCP nonce) is what recovery must rely on afterwards.

Route-change/suspend-resume monitors for live acquisitions are not implemented; profile staleness protects only future strategy selection. Ownership for NotifyRouteChange/NotifyResume is deferred to P13/P14 integration.
JournalStore is satisfied by MemoryJournal in-tree; bbolt durability wiring is the agent composition root's (P13) responsibility.

superseded_handoffs.reason: Angle A reconciliation review found a residual narrow deadlock: deliver() blocked on the 8-slot events channel under renewMu, so a blocking consumer callback that queued 8 events and then called Release deadlocked stopRenewal's join. The handoff claimed the deadlock class impossible, so the finding was fixed (unbounded lifecycleQueue; drain runs callbacks outside the queue lock; stopRenewal no longer joins the dispatcher) rather than documented. Also disposed: both dead-code leftovers (sortedKeys, hexEncode).

review_records.outcome: All 15 original findings plus batch corrections and the S7g deadlock residual verified disposed with code evidence; lifecycleQueue lock mechanics re-derived with no new deadlock or race; race+vet green. One handoff omission found and fixed by this metadata commit: the OperationID/detection-temp-journaling known-limit was claimed added but absent.

PASS. Wire codecs verified byte-exact against RFC 6887/6886 text; UPnP/SSDP/SOAP controls all present with bounded honest failure modes; all deviations conservative. Findings (ranked): MEDIUM - NAT-PMP reboot detection structurally unreachable (fresh per-transaction clients, no epoch baseline injection; the RFC 6886 §3.6 SSSoE procedure is not implemented either; fail-safe direction, manager's other LOST paths cover); LOW - PCP renew omits Suggested External IP (§11.2.1 SHOULD); NAT-PMP public-address request is 4 bytes vs RFC's 2; UPnP granted lease never learned (Query parses NewLeaseDuration but Map discards it; pacing/margin desynchronize on shortened grants); renewal jitter is one-sided 50-60% while comments say ±10% (inside RFC 6887's 1/2..5/8 band) and no 4s minimum spacing floor; PCP/NAT-PMP epoch checks are rollback-only without forward-drift; NAT-PMP Map does not refuse internal port 0 (doc says always refused); retransmission budgets deviate from RFC SHOULDs (bounded, acknowledged); TransientResult>=128 is a project rule, not RFC §7.4; SSDP response source unchecked (mitigated by LOCATION scope). Disposition: collected for the unified post-review round (fix MEDIUM symmetrically with PCP's pattern or document; compress the conservative LOWs into known_limits).
